what_it_does: Training large language models requires enormous amounts of memory. This paper compresses model weights by grouping similar values into clusters using a machine-learning technique called Differentiable KMeans (DKM), but DKM's intermediate data structures consume too much memory during training. eDKM reduces this memory overhead by deduplicating identical intermediate tensors and splitting large ones across memory partitions, enabling weight clustering of a 7-billion-parameter model using standard GPU hardware with 130x less memory overhead.
